findings.summary: `cpl self update` fails with a 404 on releases/latest/download/latest.json; `cpl self update edge` works.
findings.evidence: cpl self update -> cpl: could not download https://github.com/ryanbai1412/cp-lang/releases/latest/download/latest.json: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404

findings.summary: /setup/ says `sh -s -- --channel edge` and version `cpl 0.3.0-dev+<commit>`, getting-started says `sh -s -- --edge`, and the binary prints `cpl 0.3.0-edge+4b3d07d4`.
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/setup/ vs https://cp-lang.org/docs/guides/getting-started; cpl --version

findings.summary: /setup/ JetBrains tab says Community editions lack the language-server API, while getting-started says `cpl setup jetbrains` installs LSP4IJ in Community (which is what happens).
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/setup/ (JetBrains tab) vs https://cp-lang.org/docs/guides/getting-started

findings.summary: `cpl setup vim` reports success ('open a .cp file to start') without mentioning that LSP needs the vim-lsp plugin, which only the /setup/ Vim tab documents.
findings.evidence: cpl setup vim on a Vim with no plugins; no diagnostics until vim-lsp is cloned into ~/.vim/pack/vendor/start

findings.summary: On a freshly extracted IDEA, `cpl setup jetbrains` fails until the IDE has been launched once.
findings.evidence: cpl setup jetbrains -> cpl: no JetBrains IDE found (open one once first), or pass --dir PLUGINS

findings.summary: Opening a .cp file directly in IDEA puts it in LightEdit mode with no LSP; it has to be reopened as a trusted project.
findings.evidence: idea.sh a.cp -> LightEdit, highlighting only; 'Open in Project' -> cpl lsp starts, E0302 tooltip shows

findings.summary: In an untrusted VS Code workspace the extension is disabled and the .cp file opens as Plain Text, with no hint from CPL.
findings.evidence: code ~/edtest/a.cp in Restricted Mode -> language mode 'Plain Text'; after Trust -> 'CP Lang'

findings.summary: Codeforces problem pages return 403 to curl from the VM, so statements were read through the browser over CDP.
findings.evidence: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://codeforces.com/contest/2285/problem/A -> 403

findings.summary: `at[h].push(x)` on a missing HashMap<Int, List<Int>> key traps instead of starting an empty list, so a manual `in` branch is needed.
findings.evidence: var at: HashMap<Int, List<Int>> = HashMap(); at[5].push(1) -> error[R0001]: this key is not in the map; store with `m[k] = v` first. Wanted `at[h].push(x)`; wrote `if h in at: at[h].push(x)\nelse: at[h] = [x]`

findings.summary: Docs call `scan(a, +)` an 'inclusive running fold', but it returns a Prefix<Int, Int> of n+1 values starting with 0 that has no list methods.
findings.evidence: print(scan([1, 2, 3], +)) -> 0 1 3 6; scan(a, +).min() -> error[E0203]: Prefix<Int, Int> has no field or method `min`

findings.summary: On a `[0..n]` array, indexing scan(a, +) at n is out of domain, while on a List it has n+1 entries, so the same code behaves differently.
findings.evidence: let a: [0..5]Int = read(); let pre = scan(a, +); pre[5] -> error[R0102]: 5 is not in `D_0`, which is 0..=4

findings.summary: A zero array is `[n].filled(0)`, which reads like a one-element list; the diagnostic for `[0; n]` is good.
findings.evidence: var start = [0; n] -> error[E0503]: Rust's `[x; n]` is a fill here: `[n].filled(x)`

findings.summary: `.rev` is a getter, so `(n + 1..=m).rev()` fails to compile (clear fix hint).
findings.evidence: for k in (2..=5).rev(): ... -> error[E0304]: `rev` is read without parentheses

findings.summary: Looping while a SortedSet's maximum is >= lim needs a sentinel coalesce, because `.last!` traps on an empty set.
findings.evidence: while pool[s].last! >= lim -> error[R0301]: `!` on `None`: there is no value here; wrote `while (pool[s].last ?? 0) >= lim`, wanted e.g. `while pool[s].last is some x and x >= lim`

findings.summary: `cpl stress --explain` found the planted bug but explained nothing, because fast and brute share no variable names; a manual debug() line was needed.
findings.evidence: bug/cf2289C_bug.cp: cpl stress cf2289C_bug.cp --explain -> first differing value: none; no variable both name takes different values

findings.summary: A 30-line SortedSet small-to-large solution produces 27877 bytes of C++, which triggers the near-limit size warning.
findings.evidence: cpl submit sol/cf2289E.cp -> cpl: warning: the C++ for `cf2289E.cp` is 27877 bytes, over 24576 bytes, near the 32768-byte target

findings.summary: `cpl fetch <codeforces url>` gets 403; it works only on a saved page via `--html`.
findings.evidence: cpl fetch https://codeforces.com/contest/2289/problem/A -> curl: (22) ... 403; cpl fetch --html 2289B.html -> b.cp + b.tests

findings.summary: The `cpl new --listen` (Competitive Companion) template for multitest 2289C lacks `@!multitest`, while the `--html` template for 2289B has it.
findings.evidence: cc/c.cp created from a CC JSON POST to 127.0.0.1:10043 starts with `let n: 1..=2e5 = read()` and no @!multitest

findings.summary: The linked Competitive Companion extension can't be installed in the VM's Chromium, so the listener was driven by a hand-POSTed CC JSON.
findings.evidence: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/competitive-companion/cjnmckjndlpiamhfimnnjmnckgghkjbl -> 'Switch to Chrome to install extensions and themes'; curl -X POST 127.0.0.1:10043 -d @cc.json -> created c.cp, c.tests/ (1 sample)

findings.summary: An @check that reads a top-level solution variable is rejected only when the tests run (shown as a failing test), not by `cpl check`.
findings.evidence: comp/cf2272A.cp with `assert value(b) == base` in judge() -> checker: error[E0201]: `base` is the solution's own work: a brute or a checker shares only the input

findings.summary: Still broken: indexing a `.rev` view returns the unreversed element.
findings.evidence: let a = [5, 1, 4]; print(a.rev[0]) -> 5 (expected 4); r4/old.cp

findings.summary: Still broken: `.count()` on a List<Bool> returns the length, not the number of trues.
findings.evidence: print([true, false, true].count()) -> 3 (expected 2); r4/old.cp

findings.summary: The borrowing guide teaches `.copy()`, while the normative chapter and the move diagnostic say `.clone()`; both work.
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/docs/guides/borrowing ('let saved = a.copy()') vs /docs/ref/core/05-ownership R2 ('x.clone() is the explicit O(n) copy'); E0608 help: use `a.clone()`

findings.summary: `list.join("")` is a compile error; join is Python-style on the separator (`"".join(w)`).
findings.evidence: print(["a", "b"].join("")) -> error[E0302]: expected `Str`, found `List<Str>` help: `join` is called on the separator

findings.summary: There are two ownership chapters (a guide and the normative ref), and the guide omits rules the ref states.
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/llms.txt lists /docs/guides/borrowing and /docs/ref/core/05-ownership

findings.summary: The borrowing guide never says heap values move on `let b = a`, so I predicted a copy-required error; the ref chapter (R2) does say it.
findings.evidence: design/p1.cp: var a = [1, 2, 3]; var b = a; print(a) -> error[E0608]: `a` was already moved

findings.summary: The guide and R9 say a `mut` element lend plus a read of a possibly equal element is rejected, but the compiler accepts it (two `mut` lends are rejected with E0601).
findings.evidence: design/p4.cp: merge_into(mut counts[i], counts[j]) with no i != j proof compiles and runs (input 2 2 -> 1 2 1); design/p4b.cp swap(mut a[i], mut a[j]) -> E0601

findings.summary: The guide says a lent value 'cannot escape into ... a var' with no exception, but for plain values `var keep = owner.get()` copies and runs, as only the ref chapter says.
findings.evidence: design/p5.cp: fn get(self) -> lends Int; var keep = owner.get(); print(keep) -> 7

findings.summary: The index-spaces guide gives the motivation (positions vs cuts vs counts) but no alternatives considered or why this design won.
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/docs/guides/indices (no comparison or rationale section; contrast §13a of /docs/ref/core/05-ownership)
